humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark uses biographies of diverse people and historical figures as content to test the general factual precision of language models, rather than testing specialized disciplinary knowledge or historical research methodologies.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only evaluation that analyzes generated biographies and verifies them against Wikipedia as a reference corpus.
analytical_tasks_explanation: The benchmark evaluates long-form biography generation ('generation') by decomposing the text into short, single-assertion statements and performing fine-grained factual checking against a knowledge source ('fact_verification').

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The benchmark is specifically designed to evaluate the factual precision of long-form text generation using biography generation as its sole target task.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates several models including GPT-4, ChatGPT, InstructGPT, PerplexityAI, Alpaca, Vicuna, Dolly, Oasst-pythia, MPT-Chat, and StableLM.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses FACTSCORE (atomic-fact precision), F1-micro for individual judgments, and automated estimation error rates.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint was published in May 2023 (updated in October 2023).

summary: This paper introduces FACTSCORE, a fine-grained evaluation framework that breaks long-form text generation into distinct atomic facts and verifies each against a reliable knowledge source. The authors demonstrate its utility by evaluating various commercial and open-source LLMs on biography generation, presenting both a robust human evaluation setup and an accurate, cost-effective automated estimation model.
key_findings: State-of-the-art LLMs struggle with long-form factuality; ChatGPT only achieves a 58.3% FACTSCORE, which drops dramatically for rare entities. GPT-4 and ChatGPT are significantly more factual than public open-source models, although open models like Vicuna and Alpaca are the best within their size class.
facets_explanation: The reference factuality labels were produced by Upwork freelancers who checked whether atomic facts were supported by English Wikipedia. The atomic facts were initially generated by InstructGPT and then manually revised by the annotators. Inter-annotator disagreement was evaluated on a 10% sample and analyzed to understand error sources, treating divergence as noise rather than preserving multiple parallel valid interpretations.
